name: Rosie
positioning: An AI answering service for small businesses that learns from a Google profile and website, takes messages, books appointments and transfers calls.

pricing.model: Monthly subscription with included minutes; add-ons priced separately.
pricing.headline: Professional $49/mo (250 min), Scale $149/mo (1,000 min), Growth $299/mo (2,000 min); 7-day free trial; annual billing advertised as '2 months free'.
planNotes: Professional: 250 min, 2 message scenarios, appointment links by text, spam detection, website chat widget.
Scale: 1,000 min, calendar booking, warm and live transfers, texts to callers.
Growth: 2,000 min, waterfall transfers, custom agent training, white-glove onboarding, priority support.
Enterprise tier exists in the page's structured data, no price shown.
Annual plan dollar amounts are not shown; only the '2 months free' label.
Effective rate on the listed plans (derived, not published): about 19.6c/min on Professional down to about 15c/min on Growth.
pricing.freeTrial: 7-day free trial with all features; the vendor states no credit card is required to start.
whatIsExtra: Website texting add-on: $50/mo with 25 conversations, then $1 per additional conversation.
Website chat is listed as free with all plans.

strengths.claim: Low entry price ($49/mo) with a 7-day free trial and quick setup from a Google Business Profile and website scan.
Native iOS and Android apps, 10+ voices, English and Spanish on every call, and call summaries, transcripts and recordings.
Transfers include warm transfers where Rosie briefs the team first, and waterfall transfers that try several numbers.
Books directly into Google Calendar and Calendly (Scale plan and up), and connects to 1,000+ apps via Zapier.
Can run for after-hours or overflow calls only, via conditional call forwarding.

limitations.claim: Direct calendar booking is available on the Scale plan and higher; Professional plan users get text-a-link scheduling.
Languages stated are English and Spanish.

compliance.note: No compliance certifications found on the pages read. The FAQ lists 'Is my data secure?' but its answer was not present in the page text retrieved.

telephony.providedNumbers: Customers pick an area code for a provided number; existing business numbers are kept via call forwarding (conditional or all calls).

stepsToLeave: No export procedure was found on the pages read; the agent is built from the business website and FAQs and would be recreated.
Numbers: calls reach Rosie via forwarding from the existing number, so leaving means switching the forwarding to the new service.
Call summaries, transcripts and recordings are provided; retention period and export were not found.

bestFor: Solo owners and small local businesses that want an affordable AI receptionist with fast setup and no technical work.
unknowns: Overage behaviour when minutes run out (FAQ answer not retrievable).
Recording retention and data security statements.
Export of agent data or call records.
